feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: NPR's expanded coverage of U.S. and world politics, the latest news from Congress and the White House and elections.

entry.title: White House correspondent April Ryan reflects on reporting while under attack
entry.summary: Ryan has spent decades pressing presidents for answers. She talks about access, power, race and how asking questions put her in President Trump's crosshairs. Her new book is Notes on a Blacklash.

entry.title: ICE has quietly used this warehouse as a detention facility all summer, neighbors say
entry.summary: Throughout the summer, rumors have been bubbling in North New Jersey that ICE has quietly been using a warehouse as a detention center. NPR investigated.

entry.title: As crypto and prediction markets expand, their regulator shrinks
entry.summary: Even as the agency is tasked with drawing up new rules for crypto and prediction markets, its staffing and enforcement actions have dropped precipitously during the second Trump administration.

entry.title: Toss-ups, triage and targets: How to read the wide-open 2026 House map
entry.summary: Both parties are spending heavily in roughly 60 House districts — where Trump won by an average of 9 points in 2024 — that could be key to deciding control of the chamber, an NPR analysis finds.

entry.title: How 'Musk' director Alex Gibney became a critic
entry.summary: A trove of documents and interviews with people close to tech billionaire Elon Musk reveal a damning picture of his rise as one of the world's richest and most powerful men.

entry.title: Trump proposes Camp David-style presidential retreat at his private Florida golf club
entry.summary: President Trump said he wants to develop one of his Florida golf courses into a presidential retreat where his successors can spend quiet weekends, describing it as "sort of a Camp David."

entry.title: Trump approved the military's 1st firing squad execution since WWII. Why now?
entry.summary: The Pentagon says Nidal Hasan will be executed by firing squad in December at Fort Hood, where he killed 13 people in 2009. The announcement came days after a botched lethal injection in Tennessee.

entry.title: She got Trump's $500 check for health insurance. To her, it's a 'political stunt'
entry.summary: As checks from President Trump for health costs hit millions of mailboxes, a poll shows Americans don't trust Republicans on healthcare. Experts doubt it will move the needle and say it is likely illegal.

entry.title: 'Medicare for All' message attracts midterm voters buckling under medical bills
entry.summary: Midterm candidates are talking up Medicare for All, and in a poll 2 out of 3 Americans said they support it. The phrase speaks to a desire for radical change, though many don't really know what it is.

entry.title: Carpetbagger allegation, misplaced valor make Nevada's safe red House seat competitive
entry.summary: Northern Nevada has a reliably red congressional seat, represented by a Republican since it was drawn in the early 1980s. A complicated candidate and a potential blue wave this year could change that.
